General Who Establishes Might; governor of Nantaishan; attendant
label.zh: 建威將軍、南泰山太守、舍人

label.en: General Who Scatters the Enemy and Minister of Grand Food
court gentleman for attendance; secretariat communications attendant; supplementary gentleman
label.zh: 奉朝請，兼中書通事舍人，員外郎

label.en: General Who Pacifies the North and secretariat communications attendant
label.zh: 寧朔將軍，中書通事舍人

units.zh: 南齊書卷第五十六 列傳第三十七
units.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biographies 37
units.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biographies 37

units.zh: 紀僧真 劉係宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 呂文度
units.en: Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, and Lü Wendu
units.literal: Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Lü Wendu

units.zh: 有天象，必有人事焉。
units.en: Where there are signs in the heavens, there are corresponding events among men.
units.literal: When there are celestial signs, there must be human affairs.

units.zh: 倖臣一星，列于帝座。
units.en: The Star of Court Favorites stands arrayed beside the imperial throne.
units.literal: The Star of Favored Officials is arrayed beside the imperial throne.

units.zh: 經禮立教，亦著近臣之服。
units.en: The classics that establish ritual and instruction also prescribe the dress of those who serve close at hand.
units.literal: In establishing ritual and teaching through the classics, the attire of close ministers is also set forth.

units.zh: 親倖之義，其來已久。
units.en: The practice of granting intimate favor has a history stretching far back.
units.literal: The meaning of personal favor and trust has been longstanding.

units.zh: 爰自衰周，侯伯專命，桓、文霸主，至于戰國，寵用近習，不乏於時矣。
units.en: From the waning Zhou dynasty on, regional lords held independent power; Duke Huan and Duke Wen rose as hegemons; and by the Warring States period, rulers who pampered and relied on those nearest them were never in short supply.
units.literal: From the declining Zhou onward, marquises and earls held sole command; Duke Huan and Duke Wen became hegemons; down to the Warring States, favoring and employing close intimates was never lacking in those times.

units.zh: 漢文幸鄧通，雖錢徧天下，位止郎中。
units.en: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; though his wealth reached every corner of the empire, his office never rose above Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; although money spread throughout the realm, his rank stopped at Gentleman of the Palace.

units.zh: 孝武韓嫣、霍去病，遂至侍中大司馬。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu, favorites such as Han Yan and Huo Qubing advanced as high as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Under Emperor Wu, Han Yan and Huo Qubing rose as far as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 迄于魏、晉，世任權重，才位稍爽，而信倖唯均。
units.en: By Wei and Jin times, such men held heavy power generation after generation; talent and office no longer matched as neatly, yet imperial trust and favor were lavished on them all alike.
units.literal: Down to Wei and Jin, generation after generation they held heavy power; talent and rank grew somewhat misaligned, yet trust and favor remained evenly granted.

units.zh: 中書之職，舊掌機務。
units.en: The Secretariat had long handled the most confidential affairs of state.
units.literal: The office of the Secretariat had formerly managed state secrets.

units.zh: 漢元以令僕用事，魏明以監令專權，及在中朝，猶爲重寄。
units.en: Under Emperor Yuan of Han the Masters of Writing ran affairs; under Emperor Ming of Wei the Supervisor and Director held sole sway; and even in the central dynasties the office remained a post of the deepest trust.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han had the Masters of Writing wield power; Emperor Ming of Wei had the Supervisor and Director monopolize authority; even in the central court, the post still carried heavy trust.

units.zh: 陳准歸任上司，荀勗恨於失職。
units.en: Chen Zhun yielded his duties back to his superiors, while Xun Xu brooded over the loss of his position.
units.literal: Chen Zhun returned responsibility to his superior; Xun Xu resented the loss of his post.

units.zh: 晉令舍人位居九品，江左置通事郎，管司詔誥。
units.en: Under Jin, secretarial attendants held ninth-rank status; in the Eastern Jin court they created Communications Officers to handle imperial edicts and proclamations.
units.literal: In Jin, secretarial attendants ranked in the ninth grade; east of the Yangzi they established Communications Officers to manage imperial edicts and proclamations.

units.zh: 其後郎還爲侍郎，而舍人亦稱通事。
units.en: Later the officers were again styled Gentlemen Attendants, and secretarial attendants likewise came to be called communications officers.
units.literal: Thereafter the officers were restored as Gentlemen Attendants, while attendants were also called communications officers.

units.zh: 元帝用琅邪劉超，以謹慎居職。
units.en: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye, who kept his post through scrupulous care.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye, who held his post through careful diligence.

units.zh: 宋文世，秋當、周糾竝出寒門。
units.en: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both rose from humble households.
units.literal: In the era of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both came from humble families.

units.zh: 孝武以來，士庶雜選，如東海鮑照，以才學知名。
units.en: From Emperor Xiaowu on, men of gentry and common birth were chosen side by side, as with Bao Zhao of Donghai, famed for his talent and scholarship.
units.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu onward, gentlemen and commoners were mixed in selection; such as Bao Zhao of Donghai, who was renowned for talent and learning.

units.zh: 又用魯郡巢尚之，江夏王義恭以爲非選。
units.en: He also appointed Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery, though Prince Yigong of Jiangxia judged the choice improper.
units.literal: He also employed Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery; Prince Yigong of Jiangxia considered this an improper selection.

units.zh: 帝遣尚書二十餘牒，宣敕論辯，義恭乃歎曰：「人主誠知人。」
units.en: The emperor sent more than twenty dispatches from the Masters of Writing, issuing edicts to argue the point back and forth, until Yigong sighed and said, "The ruler truly knows how to judge men."
units.literal: The emperor sent more than twenty memorials from the Masters of Writing, proclaiming edicts to debate the matter; Yigong then sighed and said, "The sovereign truly knows men."

units.zh: 及明帝世，胡母顥、阮佃夫之徒，專爲佞倖矣。
units.en: By Emperor Ming's reign, men such as Humu Hao and Ruan Tianfu had turned the post wholly to sycophancy and private favor.
units.literal: By the era of Emperor Ming, men such as Humu Hao and Ruan Tianfu devoted themselves solely to flattery and favor.

units.zh: 齊初亦用久勞，及以親信。
units.en: At the founding of Qi as well, the court drew on men who had served long years and on those who enjoyed the ruler's personal trust.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qi they also employed those long in service, as well as personal confidants.

units.zh: 關讞表啓，發署詔敕。
units.en: They controlled access to memorials and reports and drafted and countersigned edicts and commands.
units.literal: They controlled memorials and reports, issued and signed edicts and commands.

units.zh: 頗涉辭翰者，亦爲詔文，侍郎之局，復見侵矣。
units.en: Those with some skill in letters drafted edicts as well, and the Gentlemen Attendants once again saw their domain invaded.
units.literal: Those somewhat versed in literary composition also drafted edict texts; the domain of the Gentlemen Attendants was encroached upon once again.

units.zh: 建武世，詔命殆不關中書，專出舍人。
units.en: In the Jianwu era, edicts and commands scarcely touched the Secretariat at all and came out exclusively through the secretarial attendants.
units.literal: In the Jianwu era, edicts and orders scarcely passed through the Secretariat and issued solely from the attendants.

units.zh: 省內舍人四人，所直四省，其下有主書令史，舊用武官，宋改文吏，人數無員。
units.en: Four attendants within the Secretariat each oversaw one of the four bureaus; below them stood chief clerks and record keepers. The posts had once been filled by military officers, but Song replaced them with civil clerks, and their numbers were not fixed.
units.literal: Within the Secretariat were four attendants, each responsible for one of the four bureaus; beneath them were chief clerks and record keepers; formerly military officers were used, but Song changed them to civil clerks, with no fixed number of personnel.

units.zh: 莫非左右要密，天下文簿板籍，入副其省，萬機嚴祕，有如尚書外司。
units.en: All were intimate confidants at the ruler's elbow. Copies of the empire's documents, registers, and record boards entered their bureau, and affairs of state were guarded in the strictest secrecy, as though they formed an outer branch of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: All were intimate confidants at the ruler's side; the written registers and record boards of the realm were copied into their bureau; the myriad affairs were kept in strict secrecy, like an outer office of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 領武官，有制局監，領器仗兵役，亦用寒人被恩幸者。
units.en: Military affairs were overseen by the Bureau of Equipment Supervision, which controlled arms, armor, and conscription; humble-born men who had won imperial favor served there as well.
units.literal: Overseeing military officers was the Bureau of Equipment Supervision, which commanded weapons, armor, and military service; humble-born men who had received favor were also employed there.

units.zh: 今立《倖臣篇》，以繼前史之末云。
units.en: Here we set down the treatise on court favorites, carrying on where the earlier histories left off.
units.literal: Now we establish the "Treatise on Favored Officials" to continue where the previous histories left off.

units.zh: 紀僧真，丹陽建康人也。
units.en: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jiankang in Danyang commandery.
units.literal: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jianye in Danyang.

units.zh: 僧真少隨逐征西將軍蕭思話及子惠開，皆被賞遇。
units.en: As a youth Sengzhen followed General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Hui Kai, and both men treated him with favor.
units.literal: In youth Sengzhen followed and served General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Hui Kai; both rewarded and favored him.

units.zh: 惠開性苛，僧真以微過見罰，旣而委任如舊。
units.en: Hui Kai was harsh by nature. Sengzhen was once punished for a trifling fault, but was soon entrusted again as before.
units.literal: Hui Kai was harsh by nature; Sengzhen was punished for a minor fault, yet afterward was entrusted as before.

units.zh: 及罷益州還都，不得志，僧真事之愈謹。
units.en: When Hui Kai left Yizhou and returned to the capital, bitter at his thwarted ambitions, Sengzhen served him with still greater care.
units.literal: When he left his post in Yizhou and returned to the capital, frustrated in his ambitions, Sengzhen served him all the more carefully.

units.zh: 惠開臨終歎曰：「紀僧真方當富貴，我不見也。」
units.en: On his deathbed Hui Kai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is on the verge of wealth and rank — and I shall not live to see it."
units.literal: On his deathbed Hui Kai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is about to attain wealth and honor; I shall not live to see it."

units.zh: 乃以僧真託劉秉、周顒。
units.en: He then commended Sengzhen to the care of Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.
units.literal: He then entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.

units.zh: 初，惠開在益州，土反，被圍危急，有道人謂之曰：「城圍尋解。
units.en: Earlier, while Hui Kai held Yizhou, the local tribes rebelled and he was besieged in grave danger. A Daoist told him, "The siege will soon be lifted.
units.literal: Earlier, when Hui Kai was in Yizhou, the natives rebelled and he was besieged in dire peril; a Daoist told him, "The siege will soon be lifted.

units.zh: 檀越貴門後方大興，無憂外賊也。」
units.en: Your patron's noble house will rise to great glory hereafter. You need not fear outside enemies."
units.literal: The patron's noble house will flourish greatly hereafter; do not worry about outside enemies."

units.zh: 惠開密謂僧真曰：「我子弟見在者，竝無異才。
units.en: Hui Kai told Sengzhen in confidence, "None of my sons and brothers now living has any unusual talent.
units.literal: Hui Kai secretly said to Sengzhen, "Among my sons and younger brothers now living, none has unusual talent.

units.zh: 政是道成耳。」
units.en: It is Daocheng alone who matters."
units.literal: It is truly Daocheng alone."

units.zh: 僧真憶其言，乃請事太祖。
units.en: Sengzhen kept these words in mind and therefore sought service under the Founding Emperor.
units.literal: Sengzhen remembered these words and therefore asked to serve the Founding Emperor.

units.zh: 隨從在淮陰，以閑書題，令荅遠近書疏。
units.en: Following the emperor at Huaiyin, he was set to answering correspondence from near and far because of his skill at informal writing.
units.literal: Following him at Huaiyin, because he was skilled at casual writing, he was ordered to reply to correspondence from near and far.

units.zh: 自寒官歷至太祖冠軍府參軍、主簿。
units.en: From humble posts he rose to serve as staff officer and chief clerk in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.
units.literal: From a humble office he rose through posts to Staff Officer and Chief Clerk in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.

units.zh: 僧真夢蒿艾生滿江，驚而白之。
units.en: Sengzhen dreamed that mugwort and wormwood filled the river. Alarmed, he reported the dream.
units.literal: Sengzhen dreamed that mugwort and wormwood grew covering the river; startled, he reported it.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「詩人採蕭，蕭卽艾也。
units.en: The Founding Emperor said, "The poets gather artemisia — and artemisia is wormwood.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "The poets gather artemisia; artemisia is wormwood.

units.zh: 蕭生斷流，卿勿廣言。」
units.en: Artemisia growing cuts the river's flow. Do not speak of this abroad."
units.literal: Artemisia growing cuts the flow of the river; do not speak widely of this."

units.zh: 其見親如此。
units.en: Such was the degree of intimacy he enjoyed.
units.literal: Such was the intimacy with which he was regarded.

units.zh: 元徽初，從太祖頓新亭，拒桂陽賊。
units.en: At the start of the Yuanhui era he followed the Founding Emperor in encamping at Xinting to resist the Guiyang rebels.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era, he followed the Founding Emperor in encamping at Xinting to resist the rebels of Guiyang.

units.zh: 蕭惠朗突入東門，僧真與左右共拒戰。
units.en: Xiao Huilang broke through the eastern gate, and Sengzhen fought him off together with the men at hand.
units.literal: Xiao Huilang burst through the eastern gate; Sengzhen and the attendants resisted together in battle.

units.zh: 賊退，太祖命僧真領親兵，遊邏城中。
units.en: When the rebels withdrew, the Founding Emperor ordered Sengzhen to lead his personal troops in patrolling the city.
units.literal: When the rebels withdrew, the Founding Emperor ordered Sengzhen to lead personal troops and patrol the city.

units.zh: 事寧，除南臺御史、太祖領軍功曹。
units.en: When the crisis passed, he was appointed censor of the Southern Bureau and merit officer on the Founding Emperor's staff as commander-in-chief.
units.literal: When affairs were settled, he was appointed Censor of the Southern Bureau and Merit Officer in the Founding Emperor's headquarters as Commander-in-Chief.

units.zh: 上將廢立，謀之袁粲、褚淵，僧真啓上曰：「今朝廷猖狂，人不自保，天下之望，不在袁、褚。
units.en: As the emperor prepared to depose the ruler and set another on the throne, he took counsel with Yuan Can and Chu Yuan. Sengzhen urged him, saying, "The court is now running wild and no one can feel safe. The hopes of the realm do not rest on Yuan and Chu.
units.literal: As the emperor was about to depose and enthrone, he consulted Yuan Can and Chu Yuan; Sengzhen reported to him, saying, "Now the court is reckless; no one can protect himself; the hopes of the realm do not rest on Yuan and Chu.

units.zh: 明公豈得默己，坐受夷滅。
units.en: How can you remain silent and sit by while you and yours are destroyed?
units.literal: How can my lord remain silent and sit by while destruction overtakes you?

units.zh: 存亡之機，仰希熟慮。」
units.en: The question of survival or ruin hangs on this. I beg you to weigh it with care."
units.literal: The moment of survival or destruction hangs on this; I beg you to consider it carefully."

units.zh: 太祖納之。
units.en: The Founding Emperor took his advice.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor accepted this.

units.zh: 太祖欲度廣陵起兵，僧真又啓曰：「主上雖復狂釁，虐加萬民，而累世皇基，猶固盤石。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor planned to cross to Guangling and raise troops, Sengzhen urged him again: "Though the sovereign is violent and cruel and brings suffering on the people, the imperial foundation built over generations still stands firm as bedrock.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to cross to Guangling and raise troops; Sengzhen again reported, saying, "Although the sovereign is again violent and cruel, inflicting suffering on the myriad people, the imperial foundation built over generations remains firm as bedrock.

units.zh: 今百口北度，何必得俱。
units.en: If your whole household crosses north now, why must every soul go together?
units.literal: Now if a hundred mouths cross north, why must all go together?

units.zh: 縱得廣陵城，天子居深宮施號令，目明公爲逆，何以避此？
units.en: Even if you take Guangling, the Son of Heaven will remain in the deep palace issuing orders and will mark you as a rebel. How will you escape that charge?
units.literal: Even if you take Guangling city, the Son of Heaven dwells in the deep palace issuing commands, and will regard my lord as a rebel — how will you escape this?

units.zh: 如其不勝，則應北走胡中，竊謂此非萬全策也。」
units.en: And if you fail, you would have to flee north among the barbarians. I do not believe this is a plan that can truly secure your safety."
units.literal: If you do not prevail, you would have to flee north among the barbarians; I venture to say this is not a plan of complete security."

units.zh: 上曰：「卿顧家，豈能逐我行耶。」
units.en: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family. How could you follow me in this?"
units.literal: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family; how could you follow me in this?"

units.zh: 僧真頓首稱無貳。
units.en: Sengzhen kowtowed and swore he would not waver.
units.literal: Sengzhen bowed his head to the ground and declared he would not waver.

units.zh: 昇明元年，除員外郎，帶東武城令。
units.en: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed supplementary gentleman, with concurrent duty as magistrate of Dongwucheng.
units.literal: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed Supplementary Gentleman, concurrently serving as magistrate of Dongwucheng.

units.zh: 尋除給事中、邵陵王參軍。
units.en: Soon afterward he was made gentleman attendant and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Gentleman Attendant and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.

units.zh: 太祖坐東府高樓，望石頭城，僧真在側。
units.en: The Founding Emperor sat in the high tower of the Eastern Headquarters, gazing toward Stone City, with Sengzhen at his side.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor sat in the high tower of the Eastern Headquarters, gazing at Stone City; Sengzhen was at his side.

units.zh: 上曰：「諸將勸我誅袁、劉，我意不欲便爾。」
units.en: The emperor said, "My generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu, but I am not inclined to act so hastily."
units.literal: The emperor said, "The generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu; my mind is not inclined to do so immediately."

units.zh: 及沈攸之事起，從太祖入朝堂。
units.en: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, he followed the Founding Emperor into the court hall.
units.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, he followed the Founding Emperor into the court hall.

units.zh: 石頭反夜，太祖遣衆軍掩討。
units.en: Stone City rose in revolt that night, and the Founding Emperor sent his armies to strike by surprise.
units.literal: Stone City rebelled by night; the Founding Emperor sent the armies to strike in surprise.

units.zh: 宮城中望石頭火光及呌聲甚盛，人懷不測。
units.en: From within the palace city they could see the blaze at Stone City and hear the clamor of battle. No one knew what to expect.
units.literal: Within the palace city they watched the fires and shouting at Stone City, which were very loud; people harbored uncertainty.

units.zh: 僧真謂衆曰：「呌聲不絕，是必官軍所攻。
units.en: Sengzhen told those around him, "The shouting never stops — that can only mean our own armies are attacking.
units.literal: Sengzhen said to the crowd, "The shouting does not cease; this must be the government armies attacking.

units.zh: 火光起者，賊不容自燒其城，此必官軍勝也。」
units.en: As for the flames, the rebels would never burn their own city. This can only mean our armies have won."
units.literal: Where fires rise, the rebels would not burn their own city; this must mean the government armies have won."

units.zh: 尋而啓石頭平。
units.en: Before long a report arrived that Stone City had been pacified.
units.literal: Soon a report came that Stone City was pacified.

units.zh: 上出頓新亭，使僧真領千人在帳內。
units.en: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and placed a thousand men under Sengzhen's command within the camp enclosure.
units.literal: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and ordered Sengzhen to lead a thousand men within the camp enclosure.

units.zh: 初，上在領軍府，令僧真學上手迹下名，至是報荅書疏，皆付僧真，上觀之，笑曰：「我亦不復能別也。」
units.en: Earlier, while still at the commander-in-chief's headquarters, the emperor had Sengzhen learn to imitate his hand in signing his name. Now all replies to letters and memorials were entrusted to Sengzhen. The emperor looked them over and laughed. "Even I can no longer tell the difference," he said.
units.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at the headquarters of the Commander-in-Chief, he had Sengzhen learn his own hand in signing his name; now replies to letters and memorials were all entrusted to Sengzhen; the emperor looked at them and laughed, saying, "I too can no longer tell the difference."

units.zh: 初，上在淮陰治城，得一錫趺，大數尺，下有篆文，莫能識者。
units.en: Earlier, while building the city at Huaiyin, the emperor unearthed a tin pedestal several feet across. Seal script was inscribed beneath it, but no one could read it.
units.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was building the city at Huaiyin, he obtained a tin pedestal several feet in size; beneath it was seal script that no one could read.

units.zh: 僧真曰：「何須辨此文字，此自久遠之物，九錫之徵也。」
units.en: Sengzhen said, "Why trouble to read these characters? The object itself is ancient — a sign of the Nine Bestowals."
units.literal: Sengzhen said, "Why need we decipher these characters? This is itself an object of great antiquity — a sign of the Nine Bestowals."

units.zh: 太祖曰：「卿勿妄言。」
units.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Do not speak rashly."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Do not speak rashly."

units.zh: 及上將拜齊公，已剋日，有楊袓之謀於臨軒作難。
units.en: When the emperor was about to receive investiture as Duke of Qi, with the day already set, Yang Zuzhi plotted an attack at the audience hall.
units.literal: When the emperor was about to receive investiture as Duke of Qi, the day already fixed, Yang Zuzhi plotted to make trouble at the audience hall.

units.zh: 僧真更請上選吉辰，尋而祖之事覺。
units.en: Sengzhen again asked the emperor to choose a more auspicious day. Before long Zuzhi's plot was discovered.
units.literal: Sengzhen again asked the emperor to choose an auspicious day; soon Zuzhi's plot was discovered.

units.zh: 上曰：「無卿言，亦當致小狼狽，此亦何異呼遝之冰。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Even without your warning I would have been put to some embarrassment. This is no different from the ice at Hulao."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Without your words, I would still have met with some embarrassment; this is no different from the ice of Hulao."

units.zh: 轉齊國中書舍人。
units.en: He was transferred to the post of secretariat attendant of the State of Qi.
units.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Attendant of the State of Qi.

units.zh: 建元初，帶東燕令，封新陽縣男，三百戶。
units.en: At the start of Jianyuan he concurrently served as magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county with three hundred households.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he concurrently served as magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county with three hundred households.

units.zh: 轉羽林監，加建威將軍，遷尚書主客郎，太尉中兵參軍，令如故。
units.en: He was transferred to supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and promoted to gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions and central army staff officer to the Grand Commandant, retaining his magistracy.
units.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions and central army staff officer to the Grand Commandant, retaining his magistracy.

units.zh: 復以本官兼中書舍人。
units.en: Again, while retaining his original office, he concurrently served as secretariat attendant.
units.literal: Again, on the basis of his original office he concurrently served as Secretariat Attendant.

units.zh: 太祖疾甚，令僧真典遺詔。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor was gravely ill, he ordered Sengzhen to draft the death testament.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor was gravely ill, he ordered Sengzhen to draft the death testament.

units.zh: 永明元年，寧喪，起爲建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又爲舍人，本官如故。
units.en: In the first year of Yongming, after completing mourning, he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might; soon he was appointed governor of Nantaishan, again served as attendant, and retained his former offices.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongming, after completing mourning, he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might; soon he was appointed governor of Nantaishan, and again served as attendant, retaining his former offices.

units.zh: 領諸王第事。
units.en: He oversaw affairs of the princes' mansions.
units.literal: He oversaw affairs of the princes' mansions.

units.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風。
units.en: Sengzhen's appearance and speech were refined, with a true scholar's bearing.
units.literal: Sengzhen's features and speech were elegant, with a true scholar's bearing.

units.zh: 世祖嘗目送之，笑曰：「人何必計門戶，紀僧真常貴人所不及。」
units.en: Emperor Wu once watched him depart and said with a laugh, "Why must one count family standing? Ji Sengzhen is often what the highly born cannot match."
units.literal: Emperor Wu once followed him with his eyes and said with a laugh, "Why must one count family standing? Ji Sengzhen is often what the highly born cannot match."

units.zh: 諸權要中，最被盻遇。
units.en: Among the powerful he was the most favored with attentive regard.
units.literal: Among the powerful he was most favored with attentive regard.

units.zh: 除越騎校尉，餘官如故。
units.en: He was appointed colonel of the Yue Cavalry; his other offices remained as before.
units.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the Yue Cavalry; his other offices remained as before.

units.zh: 出爲建武將軍，建康令。
units.en: He went out as General Establishing Might and magistrate of Jiankang.
units.literal: He went out as General Establishing Might and magistrate of Jiankang.

units.zh: 還除左右郎將，泰山太守。
units.en: On returning he was appointed left and right commander of the palace guards and governor of Taishan.
units.literal: On returning he was appointed Left and Right Commander of the Palace Guards and governor of Taishan.

units.zh: 加先驅使。
units.en: He was given the additional post of vanguard commissioner.
units.literal: He was given the additional post of vanguard commissioner.

units.zh: 尋除前軍將軍。
units.en: Soon he was appointed General of the Vanguard.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Vanguard.

units.zh: 遭母喪，開冢得五色兩頭蛇。
units.en: When his mother died, opening the tomb revealed a five-colored two-headed snake.
units.literal: When his mother died, in opening the tomb they found a five-colored two-headed snake.

units.zh: 世祖崩，僧真號泣思慕。
units.en: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in longing.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in longing.

units.zh: 明帝以僧真歷朝驅使，建武元年，除游擊將軍，兼司農，待之如舊。
units.en: Because Sengzhen had served as a dispatch runner through successive reigns, in the first year of Jianwu Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Scatters the Enemy with concurrent charge as Minister of Grand Food and treated him as before.
units.literal: Because Sengzhen had served through successive reigns as a dispatch runner, in the first year of Jianwu Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Scatters the Enemy with concurrent charge as Minister of Grand Food, treating him as before.

units.zh: 欲令僧真治郡，僧真啓進其弟僧猛爲鎮蠻護軍、晉熙太守。
units.en: When the emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, Sengzhen memorialized to advance his younger brother Sengmeng as protector-general for pacifying the barbarians and governor of Jinxi.
units.literal: When the emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, Sengzhen memorialized to advance his younger brother Sengmeng as protector-general who pacifies the barbarians and governor of Jinxi.

units.zh: 永泰元年，除司農卿。
units.en: In the first year of Yongtai he was appointed Minister of Grand Food.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was appointed Minister of Grand Food.

units.zh: 明帝崩，掌山陵事。
units.en: When Emperor Ming died, he oversaw matters of the imperial tomb.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he oversaw matters of the imperial mound-tomb.

units.zh: 出爲廬陵內史，年五十五，卒。
units.en: He was sent out as interior scribe of Luling and died at the age of fifty-five.
units.literal: He went out as interior scribe of Luling; at the age of fifty-five he died.

units.zh: 宋世道人楊法持，與太祖有舊。
units.en: During Song times the Daoist Yang Fachi had long-standing ties with the Founding Emperor.
units.literal: In Song times the Daoist Yang Fachi had old ties with the Founding Emperor.

units.zh: 元徽末，宣傳密謀。
units.en: At the end of the Yuanhui era he helped spread secret plots.
units.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he spread secret plots.

units.zh: 昇明中，以爲僧正。
units.en: During the Shengming era he was made superintendent of monks.
units.literal: During Shengming he was made Superintendent of Monks.

units.zh: 建元初，罷道，爲寧朔將軍，封州陵縣男，三百戶。
units.en: At the start of Jianyuan he left the religious life, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling county with three hundred households.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he left the religious life, was made General Who Pacifies the North, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling county with three hundred households.

units.zh: 二年，虜圍朐山，遣法持爲軍主，領支軍救援。
units.en: In the second year, when the barbarians besieged Qushan, Fachi was sent as army commander to lead a relief detachment.
units.literal: In the second year, when the barbarians besieged Qushan, Fachi was sent as army commander to lead a supporting force in relief.

units.zh: 永明四年，坐役使將客，奪其鮭稟，削封。
units.en: In the fourth year of Yongming he was stripped of his enfeoffment for forcing a traveling guest into service and seizing his salmon ration.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, for employing and mistreating a traveling guest and seizing his salmon ration, his enfeoffment was revoked.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 劉係宗，丹陽人也。
units.en: Liu Xizong was a native of Danyang.
units.literal: Liu Xizong was a native of Danyang.

units.zh: 少便書畫，爲宋竟陵王誕子景粹侍書。
units.en: As a youth he was skilled in writing and painting and served as calligrapher to Jing Cui, son of Prince Dan of Jingling of Song.
units.literal: In youth he was skilled at writing and painting and served as calligrapher to Jing Cui, son of Prince Dan of Jingling of Song.

units.zh: 誕舉兵廣陵，城內皆死，敕沈慶之赦係宗，以爲東宮侍書。
units.en: When Dan raised troops at Guangling everyone in the city was put to death, but an edict ordered Shen Qingzhi to pardon Xizong, who was then appointed calligrapher to the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: When Dan raised troops at Guangling, all within the city were put to death; an edict from Shen Qingzhi pardoned Xizong and appointed him calligrapher to the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 泰始中，爲主書。
units.en: During the Taishi era he served as chief clerk.
units.literal: During Taishi he served as chief clerk.

units.zh: 以寒官累遷至勳品。
units.en: From humble posts he rose step by step to meritorious rank.
units.literal: From a humble office he was repeatedly promoted to meritorious rank.

units.zh: 元徽初，爲奉朝請，兼中書通事舍人，員外郎。
units.en: At the start of the Yuanhui era he was made court gentleman for attendance, with concurrent posts as secretariat communications attendant and supplementary gentleman.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance, concurrently Secretariat Communications Attendant and Supplementary Gentleman.

units.zh: 封始興南亭侯，食邑三百七十戶。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing, with a fief of three hundred seventy households.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing, with a fief of three hundred seventy households.

units.zh: 帶秣陵令。
units.en: He concurrently served as magistrate of Moling.
units.literal: He concurrently served as magistrate of Moling.

units.zh: 太祖廢蒼梧，明旦，呼正直舍人虞整，醉不能起，係宗歡喜奉命。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor deposed Emperor Cangwu, the next morning he summoned the upright attendant Yu Zheng, who was too drunk to rise. Xizong gladly took the order in his place.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor deposed Cangwu, the next morning he summoned the upright attendant Yu Zheng, who was drunk and could not rise; Xizong gladly accepted the command.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「今天地重開，是卿盡力之日。」
units.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Heaven and earth open anew today. This is the day for you to give your utmost."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Today heaven and earth open anew; this is the day for you to exert yourself to the utmost."

units.zh: 使寫諸處分敕令，及四方書疏。
units.en: He had him draft all disposition orders and edicts, as well as correspondence to every quarter of the realm.
units.literal: He had him write all disposition orders and edicts, as well as correspondence to the four directions.

units.zh: 使主書十人書吏二十人配之，事皆稱旨。
units.en: He assigned him ten chief clerks and twenty writing clerks. In every matter Xizong met the emperor's wishes.
units.literal: He assigned him ten chief clerks and twenty writing clerks; in every matter he met with approval.

units.zh: 除羽林監，轉步兵校尉。
units.en: He was appointed supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and then transferred to colonel of footsoldiers.
units.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and transferred to Colonel of Footsoldiers.

units.zh: 仍除龍驤將軍，出爲海鹽令。
units.en: He was then appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and sent out to serve as magistrate of Haiyan.
units.literal: He was then appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan.

units.zh: 太祖卽位，除龍驤將軍、建康令。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.

units.zh: 永明元年，除寧朔將軍，令如故。
units.en: In the first year of Yongming he was made General Who Pacifies the North while keeping his post as magistrate.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, retaining his magistracy as before.

units.zh: 尋轉右軍將軍、淮陵太守，兼中書通事舍人。
units.en: Soon afterward he became General of the Right Army and governor of Huailing, with concurrent duty as secretariat communications attendant.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Right Army and governor of Huailing, concurrently Secretariat Communications Attendant.

units.zh: 母喪自解，起爲寧朔將軍，復本職。
units.en: He resigned on his mother's death, then on returning from mourning was restored as General Who Pacifies the North and resumed his former posts.
units.literal: On his mother's death he resigned of his own accord; on mourning's end he was restored as General Who Pacifies the North and resumed his former duties.

units.zh: 四年，白賊唐宇之起，宿衞兵東討，遣係宗隨軍慰勞，徧至遭賊郡縣。
units.en: In the fourth year the White-bandit rebel Tang Yuzhi rose. The palace guard marched east to suppress him, and Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards, visiting every commandery and county the rebels had ravaged.
units.literal: In the fourth year the White-bandit rebel Tang Yuzhi rose; the palace guard marched east to suppress him, and Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards, reaching every commandery and county that had suffered the rebels.

units.zh: 百姓被驅逼者，悉無所問，還復民伍。
units.en: Commoners who had been driven into service were not punished and were restored to civilian life.
units.literal: Common people who had been driven and compelled were all left unpunished and restored to civilian status.

units.zh: 係宗還，上曰：「此段有征無戰，以時平蕩，百姓安怗，甚快也。」
units.en: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "This campaign brought expedition without battle. The disturbance was pacified in good time and the people are at peace — I am most pleased."
units.literal: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "In this campaign there was expedition without battle; the disturbance was pacified in good time and the people are settled in peace — most gratifying."

units.zh: 賜係宗錢帛。
units.en: He rewarded Xizong with money and silks.
units.literal: He bestowed money and silks on Xizong.

units.zh: 上欲脩治白下城，難於動役。
units.en: The emperor wished to repair Baixia city but hesitated to mobilize labor for the project.
units.literal: The emperor wished to repair and improve Baixia city but found it difficult to mobilize labor.

units.zh: 係宗啓謫役東民丁隨宇之爲逆者，上從之。
units.en: Xizong proposed assigning corvée labor from eastern households that had followed Yuzhi in rebellion, and the emperor agreed.
units.literal: Xizong reported that corvée labor from eastern households that had followed Yuzhi in rebellion should be assigned to the work; the emperor agreed.

units.zh: 後車駕講武，上履行白下城，曰：「劉係宗爲國家得此一城。」
units.en: Later, during an imperial martial review, the emperor walked along Baixia city and said, "Liu Xizong won this city for the state."
units.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage reviewed the troops in martial display, the emperor walked along Baixia city and said, "Liu Xizong won this city for the state."

units.zh: 永明中，虜使書常令係宗題答，祕書書局皆隷之。
units.en: During Yongming, replies to letters from barbarian envoys were often entrusted to Xizong for drafting, and the secretariat's writing offices were all placed under his supervision.
units.literal: During Yongming, when barbarian envoys sent letters, Xizong was often made to inscribe the replies; the secretariat's writing offices were all placed under him.

units.zh: 再爲少府，遷游擊將軍、魯郡太守。
units.en: He twice served as Minister of the Palace Parks, then was promoted to General Who Scatters the Enemy and governor of Lu commandery.
units.literal: He twice served as Minister of the Palace Parks, then was transferred to General Who Scatters the Enemy and governor of Lu commandery.

units.zh: 鬱林卽位，除驍騎將軍，仍除寧朔將軍、宣城太守。
units.en: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xizong was made General of Valiant Cavalry and then concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Xuancheng.
units.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, then concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Xuancheng.

units.zh: 係宗久在朝省，閑於職事。
units.en: Xizong had long served in the court offices and was thoroughly skilled in official business.
units.literal: Xizong had long served in the court offices and was skilled in official business.

units.zh: 明帝曰：「學士不堪治國，唯大讀書耳。
units.en: Emperor Ming said, "Scholars cannot govern a state — they only read vast numbers of books.
units.literal: Emperor Ming said, "Scholars are unfit to govern the state; they only read many books.

units.zh: 一劉係宗足持如此輩五百人。」
units.en: A single Liu Xizong is worth five hundred of them."
units.literal: One Liu Xizong is enough to manage five hundred such men."

units.zh: 其重吏事如此。
units.en: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
units.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

units.zh: 建武二年，卒官，年七十七。
units.en: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at the age of seventy-seven.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at the age of seventy-seven.

units.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。
units.en: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.
units.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

units.zh: 宋大明世，出身爲小史，歷齋幹扶。
units.en: In the Daming era of Song he began as a petty clerk and rose through posts as orderly and attendant.
units.literal: In the Daming era of Song he first served as a petty clerk and passed through posts as orderly and attendant.

units.zh: 孝武末年，作酒法，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。
units.en: In Emperor Xiaowu's last years he instituted drinking regulations with excessive flogging. On a hunting expedition south of the Yangzi he selected one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress, all men of wealthy households, and took them to the southern regions; more than half were flogged.
units.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu he instituted drinking regulations with excessive flogging; on a hunting expedition to the lands south of the Yangzi he selected one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress, all handsome men from wealthy households, and took them to the southern regions; more than half received the lash.

units.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啓出家得爲道人。
units.en: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized the opportunity to petition to leave the world and become a Daoist priest.
units.literal: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized the opportunity to report that he wished to leave the world and become a Daoist priest.

units.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，用爲兖州刺史孟次陽典籤。
units.en: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he left the religious life, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, and was appointed chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, governor of Yanzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the religious life, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, and was employed as chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, governor of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 累至太祖冠軍府行參軍。
units.en: He rose step by step to acting staff officer in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Staff Officer in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.

units.zh: 元徽初，除殿中將軍，爲晉熙王郢州典籤，除長兼殿中御史。
units.en: At the start of the Yuanhui era he was made General of the Palace, chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou, and chief censor of the palace with extended authority.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was appointed General of the Palace, made chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou, and appointed Chief Censor of the Palace with extended authority.

units.zh: 世祖鎮盆城，須舊驅使人，法亮求留爲上江州典籤，除南臺御史，帶松滋令。
units.en: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng and needed experienced dispatch runners, Faliang asked to stay on as chief clerk of Upper Jiangzhou, was appointed censor of the Southern Terrace, and concurrently served as magistrate of Songzi.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng and needed old dispatch runners, Faliang asked to remain as chief clerk of Upper Jiangzhou, was appointed censor of the Southern Terrace, and concurrently served as magistrate of Songzi.

units.zh: 法亮便辟解事，善於承奉，稍見委信。
units.en: Faliang was quick and capable, skilled at attendance and service, and gradually won trust and responsibility.
units.literal: Faliang was clever and capable in affairs, skilled at attending and serving, and gradually won trust and appointment.

units.zh: 從還石頭。
units.en: He followed the emperor back to Stone City.
units.literal: He followed back to Stone City.

units.zh: 建元初，度東宮主書。
units.en: At the start of Jianyuan he was transferred to chief clerk of the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Eastern Palace chief clerk.

units.zh: 除奉朝請，補東宮通事舍人。
units.en: He was appointed court gentleman for attendance and made Eastern Palace communications attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and supplemented as Eastern Palace Communications Attendant.

units.zh: 世祖卽位，仍爲中書通事舍人。
units.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he continued as secretariat communications attendant.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Secretariat Communications Attendant.

units.zh: 除員外郎，帶南濟陰太守。
units.en: He was appointed supplementary gentleman and concurrently served as governor of Nanjiyin.
units.literal: He was appointed Supplementary Gentleman and concurrently served as governor of Nanjiyin.

units.zh: 永明元年，除龍驤將軍。
units.en: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry.

units.zh: 明年，詔曰：「茹法亮近在盆城，頻使銜命，內宣朝旨，外慰三軍。
units.en: The next year an edict said: "Ru Faliang was recently at Pencheng, repeatedly bearing imperial commands, proclaiming the court's will within and comforting the armies without.
units.literal: The next year an edict said: "Ru Faliang was recently at Pencheng, repeatedly bearing imperial commands, proclaiming court directives within and comforting the three armies without.

units.zh: 義勇齊奮，人百其氣。
units.en: With righteous courage all strove as one; each man fought with redoubled spirit.
units.literal: With righteous courage all strove together; each man gave a hundredfold of his spirit.

units.zh: 險阻艱難，心力俱盡。
units.en: Through peril and hardship he gave his utmost in heart and strength.
units.literal: Through peril and hardship he exhausted heart and strength alike.

units.zh: 宜沾茅土，以甄忠績。」
units.en: He should receive a fief to reward his loyal service."
units.literal: He should be granted a fief of soil to distinguish his loyal achievement."

units.zh: 封望蔡縣男，食邑三百戶。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of three hundred households.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of three hundred households.

units.zh: 轉給事中，羽林監。
units.en: He was transferred to gentleman attendant and supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

units.zh: 七年，除臨淮太守，轉竟陵王司徒中兵參軍。
units.en: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Linhuai and transferred to central army staff officer to the Minister of State on the Prince of Jingling's staff.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Linhuai and transferred to central army staff officer to the Minister of State for the Prince of Jingling.

units.zh: 巴東王子響於荊州殺僚佐，上遣軍西上，使法亮宣旨慰勞，安撫子響。
units.en: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou. The emperor sent armies west and dispatched Faliang to proclaim the imperial will, offer comfort, and pacify the prince.
units.literal: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou; the emperor sent armies west and dispatched Faliang to proclaim the imperial will, offer comfort, and pacify Zixiang.

units.zh: 法亮至江津，子響呼法亮，法亮疑畏不肯往。
units.en: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.
units.literal: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, would not go.

units.zh: 又求見傳詔，法亮又不遣。
units.en: The prince again asked to see the edict-bearer, but Faliang would not send him in.
units.literal: Zixiang again asked to see the edict-bearer, but Faliang would not send him in.

units.zh: 故子響怒，遣兵破尹略軍。
units.en: The prince grew angry and sent troops to defeat the army of Yin Lue.
units.literal: Therefore Zixiang grew angry and sent troops to defeat the army of Yin Lue.

units.zh: 事平，法亮至江陵，刑賞處分，皆稱敕斷決。
units.en: When the affair was settled, Faliang reached Jiangling and decided punishments, rewards, and dispositions all in the name of imperial command.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, Faliang reached Jiangling; punishments, rewards, and dispositions were all decided in the name of imperial command.

units.zh: 軍還，上悔誅子響，法亮被責。
units.en: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang and blamed Faliang.
units.literal: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang and Faliang was blamed.

units.zh: 少時，親任如舊。
units.en: Before long he enjoyed the emperor's trust and employment as before.
units.literal: Before long he was trusted and employed as before.

units.zh: 鬱林卽位，除步兵校尉。
units.en: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Faliang was appointed colonel of footsoldiers.
units.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Faliang was appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers.

units.zh: 延興元年，爲前軍將軍。
units.en: In the first year of Yanxing he was made General of the Vanguard.
units.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was made General of the Vanguard.

units.zh: 延昌殿爲世祖陰室，藏諸御服。
units.en: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, where the imperial wardrobe was kept.
units.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, where all imperial garments were stored.

units.zh: 二少帝竝居西殿，高宗卽位住東齋，開陰室出世祖白紗帽防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。
units.en: The two young emperors both lived in the western hall. When Emperor Gao took the throne he lodged in the eastern studio, opened the private chamber, and brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and self-defense knife. Faliang sobbed and wept.
units.literal: The two young emperors both dwelt in the western hall; when Emperor Gao took the throne he lodged in the eastern studio, opened the private chamber, and brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and self-defense knife; Faliang sobbed and wept.

units.zh: 除游擊將軍。
units.en: He was appointed General Who Scatters the Enemy.
units.literal: He was appointed General Who Scatters the Enemy.

units.zh: 高武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。
units.en: Few of Emperor Gao Wu's old associates still survived. Because Faliang handled documentary affairs at the secretariat, he was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained unchanged.
units.literal: Few of Emperor Gao Wu's old associates still survived; because Faliang was in charge of documentary affairs at the secretariat, he was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained as before.

units.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰。
units.en: In the first year of Yongtai, when Wang Jingze's revolt was put down, Faliang again received orders to proclaim imperial comfort.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, when Wang Jingze's affair was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort.

units.zh: 出法亮爲大司農，中書勢利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受，旣而代人已致，法亮垂涕而出。
units.en: Faliang was transferred out to serve as Minister of Grand Food. The Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and he was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined the transfer, but soon his replacement had arrived, and Faliang left in tears.
units.literal: Faliang was sent out as Minister of Grand Food; the Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and Faliang was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined and would not accept, but soon his replacement had arrived, and Faliang went out in tears.

units.zh: 年六十四，卒官。
units.en: He died in office at the age of sixty-four.
units.literal: At the age of sixty-four he died in office.

units.zh: 呂文顯，臨海人也。
units.en: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.
units.literal: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.

units.zh: 初爲宋孝武齋幹直長。
units.en: He first served as chief orderly of the fasting guard under Emperor Xiaowu of Song.
units.literal: Initially he served as chief orderly of the fasting guard under Emperor Xiaowu of Song.

units.zh: 昇明初，爲太祖錄尚書省事，累位至殿中侍御史，羽林監，帶蘭陵丞、令，龍驤將軍，秣陵令。
units.en: At the start of Shengming he served in the Founding Emperor's secretariat for recording master-of-writing affairs and rose through posts as attendant censor of the palace, supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, concurrently assistant magistrate and magistrate of Lanling, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and magistrate of Moling.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he served in the Founding Emperor's Secretariat for Recording Master of Writing affairs, and was repeatedly promoted to attendant censor of the palace, supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, concurrently assistant magistrate and magistrate of Lanling, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and magistrate of Moling.

units.zh: 封劉陽縣男。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Liuyang county.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Liuyang county.

units.zh: 永明元年，除寧朔將軍，中書通事舍人，本官如故。
units.en: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and secretariat communications attendant, retaining his former offices.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Secretariat Communications Attendant, retaining his former offices.

units.zh: 文顯治事以刻覈被知。
units.en: Wenxian became known for administering affairs with harsh rigor.
units.literal: Wenxian became known for handling affairs with harsh rigor.

units.zh: 三年，帶南清河太守。
units.en: In the third year he concurrently served as governor of Nanqinghe.
units.literal: In the third year he concurrently served as governor of Nanqinghe.

units.zh: 與茹法亮等迭出入爲舍人，竝見親倖。
units.en: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns serving as secretariat attendants, and all enjoyed the emperor's intimate favor.
units.literal: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns entering and leaving as attendants, and all were personally favored.

units.zh: 四方餉遺，歲各數百萬，竝造大宅，聚山開池。
units.en: Gifts from every quarter brought them several million a year apiece. They all built great mansions, heaped up artificial hills, and opened ornamental pools.
units.literal: Gifts from the four directions amounted to several million each year; they all built great mansions, heaped up hills, and opened pools.

units.zh: 五年，爲建康令，轉長水校尉，歷帶南泰山、南譙太守，尋爲司徒中兵參軍，淮南太守，直舍人省。
units.en: In the fifth year he became magistrate of Jiankang, then colonel of the Long River, and successively held concurrent governorships of Nantaishan and Nanqiao. Soon afterward he was made central army staff officer to the Minister of State, governor of Huainan, and attached to the attendants' bureau.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was magistrate of Jiankang, then transferred to Colonel of the Long River, successively concurrently governor of Nantaishan and Nanqiao, soon made Central Army Staff Officer to the Minister of State, governor of Huainan, and attached to the Attendants' Bureau.

units.zh: 累遷左中郎將，南東莞太守，右軍將軍。
units.en: He rose through the posts of left commander of the palace guards, governor of Nandongguan, and General of the Right Army.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Commander of the Palace Guards, governor of Nandongguan, and General of the Right Army.

units.zh: 高宗輔政，以文顯守少府，見任使。
units.en: When Emperor Gao held the regency, Wenxian was made acting Minister of the Palace Parks and was trusted with important duties.
units.literal: When Emperor Gao held regency, Wenxian was made acting Minister of the Palace Parks and was trusted and employed.

units.zh: 歷建武、永元之世，尚書右丞，少府卿。
units.en: Through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras he served as right assistant master of writing and Minister of the Palace Parks.
units.literal: Through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras he served as Right Assistant Master of Writing and Minister of the Palace Parks.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 呂文度，會稽人。
units.en: Lü Wendu was a native of Kuaiji.
units.literal: Lü Wendu was a native of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 宋世爲細作金銀庫吏，竹局匠。
units.en: During Song he served as clerk in the fine-work gold and silver treasury and as a bamboo-frame craftsman.
units.literal: In Song times he served as clerk in the fine-work gold and silver treasury and as a bamboo-frame craftsman.

units.zh: 元徽中，爲射雉典事，隨監莫脩宗上郢。
units.en: During the Yuanhui era he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting and followed Supervisor Mo Xiuzong to Ying.
units.literal: During Yuanhui he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting and followed Supervisor Mo Xiuzong to Ying.

units.zh: 世祖鎮盆城拒沈攸之，文度仍留伏事，知軍隊雜役，以此見親。
units.en: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng resisting Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained behind to serve in secret and knew the army's miscellaneous duties; for this he won the emperor's favor.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng resisting Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained behind to serve in secret, knowing the miscellaneous duties of the army; for this he was treated with favor.

units.zh: 從還都，爲石頭城監，仍度東宮。
units.en: On returning to the capital he was made supervisor of Stone City and then transferred to the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: On returning to the capital he was made supervisor of Stone City and then transferred to the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 世祖卽位，爲制局監，位至員外郎，帶南濮陽太守。
units.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Wendu was made supervisor of the Equipment Bureau, rose to supplementary gentleman, and concurrently served as governor of Nanpuyang.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Wendu was made Supervisor of the Equipment Bureau, rose to Supplementary Gentleman, and concurrently served as governor of Nanpuyang.

units.zh: 殿內軍隊及發遣外鎮人，悉關之，甚有要勢。
units.en: Palace troops and personnel dispatched to outer garrisons all passed through his hands, and he wielded great strategic power.
units.literal: Palace troops within the hall and personnel dispatched to outer garrisons all depended on him; he held great strategic power.

units.zh: 故世傳越州嘗缺，上覔一直事人往越州，文度啓其所知費延宗合旨，上卽以爲刺史。
units.en: Hence the story that when Yuezhou once lacked a governor, the emperor sought a direct attendant to send there. Wendu reported that Fei Yanzong, a man he knew, suited the emperor's wishes, and the emperor at once appointed him governor.
units.literal: Hence it was said in the world that when Yuezhou once lacked an appointee, the emperor sought a direct attendant to go to Yuezhou; Wendu reported that Fei Yanzong, whom he knew, suited the emperor's wish, and the emperor at once made him governor.

units.zh: 永明中，敕親近不得輙有申薦，人士免官，寒人鞭一百。
units.en: During Yongming an edict forbade intimates from making recommendations at will: gentlemen were dismissed from office, humble men were flogged one hundred strokes.
units.literal: During Yongming an edict forbade intimates from making recommendations at will; gentlemen were dismissed from office, humble men were flogged one hundred strokes.

units.zh: 上性尊嚴，呂文顯嘗在殿側咳聲高，上使茹法亮訓詰之，以爲不敬，故左右畏威承意，非所隷莫敢有言也。
units.en: The emperor was stern by nature. Lü Wenxian once coughed loudly beside the throne, and the emperor had Ru Faliang reprimand him for disrespect. Thereafter those at the emperor's side feared his authority and complied with his wishes, and none outside their jurisdiction dared speak up.
units.literal: The emperor was stern by nature; Lü Wenxian once coughed loudly at the side of the hall; the emperor had Ru Faliang reprimand him as disrespectful; therefore those at his side feared his authority and complied with his wishes, and none outside their jurisdiction dared speak.

units.zh: 時茹法亮掌雜驅使簿，及宣通密敕；
units.en: At that time Ru Faliang controlled miscellaneous service registers and the proclamation and transmission of secret edicts;
units.literal: At that time Ru Faliang controlled miscellaneous service registers and the proclamation and transmission of secret edicts;

units.zh: 呂文顯掌穀帛事；
units.en: Lü Wenxian controlled grain and silk affairs;
units.literal: Lü Wenxian controlled grain and silk affairs;

units.zh: 其餘舍人無別任。
units.en: the other attendants had no separate duties.
units.literal: the other attendants had no separate duties.

units.zh: 虎賁中郎將潘敞掌監功作。
units.en: Commander of the Tiger Guards Pan Chang supervised construction work.
units.literal: Commander of the Tiger Guards Pan Chang supervised construction work.

units.zh: 上使造禪靈寺新成，車駕臨視，甚悅。
units.en: The emperor had the new Chanling Temple built. When the imperial carriage came to inspect it, he was greatly pleased.
units.literal: The emperor had the new Chanling Temple built; when the imperial carriage came to inspect it, he was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 敞喜，要呂文顯私登寺南門樓，上知之，繫敞上方，而出文顯爲南譙郡，久之乃復。
units.en: Chang rejoiced and invited Lü Wenxian to climb privately to the temple's south gate tower. When the emperor learned of it, he imprisoned Chang in the imperial residence and sent Wenxian out as governor of Nanqiao commandery. Only after a long time was Wenxian restored.
units.literal: Chang rejoiced and invited Lü Wenxian to climb privately to the south gate tower of the temple; when the emperor learned of it, he imprisoned Chang in the imperial residence and sent Wenxian out as governor of Nanqiao; only after a long time was he restored.

units.zh: 濟陽江瞿曇、吳興沈徽孚等，以士流舍人通事而已，無權利。
units.en: Jiang Qutan of Jiyang, Shen Huifu of Wuxing, and others served as gentlemen communications attendants and merely handled routine matters, with no power or profit.
units.literal: Jiang Qutan of Jiyang, Shen Huifu of Wuxing, and others, as gentlemen serving as communications attendants, merely handled routine matters and held no power or profit.

units.zh: 徽孚粗有筆札。
units.en: Huifu had some skill as a writer.
units.literal: Huifu had some skill in writing.

units.zh: 建武中文詔，多其辭也。
units.en: During Jianwu many literary edicts bore his phrasing.
units.literal: During Jianwu many literary edicts bore his phrasing.

units.zh: 官至黃門郎。
units.en: He rose to the post of gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: He reached the office of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 史臣曰：中世已來，宰御天下，萬機碎密，不關外司。
units.en: The historian says: From the middle ages onward, those who governed the realm kept the myriad affairs in minute detail, and nothing passed through the outer offices.
units.literal: The historian says: From the middle ages onward, those who governed the realm held the myriad affairs in minute detail, and nothing passed through the outer offices.

units.zh: 尚書八座五曹，各有恒任，係以九卿六府，事存副職。
units.en: The eight seats and five bureaus of the Masters of Writing each had fixed duties, joined to the nine ministers and six courts with their supporting offices.
units.literal: The eight seats and five bureaus of the Masters of Writing each had fixed duties; joined to the nine ministers and six courts, affairs were held in duplicate posts.

units.zh: 咸皆冠冕搢紳，任疏人貴，伏奏之務旣寢，趨走之勞亦息。
units.en: All were crowned officials of the gentry class, remote in duty and exalted in rank. The task of presenting memorials prostrate had long ceased, and the labor of running errands had ended as well.
units.literal: All were crowned officials and gentry; their duties were remote and their persons exalted; the task of presenting memorials prostrate had already ceased, and the labor of running errands had also ended.

units.zh: 關宣所寄，屬當有歸，通驛內外，切自音旨。
units.en: What passed through the barrier of proclamation had its proper place, and couriers moved within and without, all closely following the ruler's own words.
units.literal: What was entrusted to the barrier and proclamation had its proper place; couriers passed within and without, all closely following the ruler's own words.

units.zh: 若夫環纓斂笏，俯仰晨昏，贍幄座而竦躬，陪蘭檻而高眄，探求恩色，習睹威顏，遷蘭變鮑，久而彌信，因城社之固，執開壅之機。
units.en: As for those who adjusted their tassels and held their tablets, bowing morning and evening, attending the curtained throne with straightened bodies and standing beside the orchid balustrade with eyes raised, seeking every sign of favor and growing accustomed to the august countenance — changing like orchids and abalone with long familiarity — they relied on the solidity of the court's foundations and grasped the mechanism that opens and blocks access to power.
units.literal: As for those who adjusted their tassels and held their tablets, bowing morning and evening, attending the curtained seat with straightened bodies, standing beside the orchid balustrade and gazing upward, seeking out expressions of favor, growing accustomed to the august countenance, changing like orchids and abalone with long familiarity, relying on the solidity of city altars, they grasped the mechanism that opens and blocks.

units.zh: 長主君世，振裘持領，賞罰事殷，能不踰漏，宮省咳唾，義必先知。
units.en: When the ruler held the throne for long years, they shook the fur and held the collar of power. Rewards and punishments were numerous, yet nothing escaped their notice; a cough or spit in the palace offices they knew beforehand by obligation.
units.literal: When the ruler was long on the throne, they shook the fur and held the collar; rewards and punishments were numerous, yet nothing escaped their notice; a cough or spit in the palace offices they necessarily knew beforehand.

units.zh: 故能窺盈縮於望景，獲驪珠於龍睡。
units.en: Thus they could read waxing and waning from observing shadows, and seize the black dragon's pearl while it slept.
units.literal: Thus they could discern waxing and waning from observing shadows, and obtain the black dragon's pearl while it slept.

units.zh: 坐歸聲勢，卧震都鄙。
units.en: Seated, their renown and power gathered about them; reclining, they shook the capital and the countryside.
units.literal: Seated, their renown and power returned to them; reclining, they shook capital and countryside.

units.zh: 賄賂日積，苞苴歲通，富擬公侯，威行州郡。
units.en: Bribes accumulated day by day and gifts passed year by year. Their wealth rivaled that of marquises and earls, and their authority ran through provinces and commanderies.
units.literal: Bribes accumulated day by day, gifts passed year by year; their wealth rivaled marquises and earls, their authority ran through provinces and commanderies.

units.zh: 制局小司，專典兵力，雲陛天居，亙設蘭錡，羽林精卒，重屯廣衞。
units.en: The petty offices of the Equipment Bureau specialized in managing military strength. Cloud steps and heavenly dwellings were set throughout with orchid halberds, and elite Feathered Forest troops were heavily stationed in broad guard.
units.literal: The petty offices of the Equipment Bureau specialized in managing military strength; cloud steps and heavenly dwellings were set throughout with orchid halberds; elite Feathered Forest troops were heavily stationed in broad guard.

units.zh: 至于元戎啓轍，式候還麾，遮迾清道，神行案轡，督察來往，馳騖輦轂，驅役分部，親承几案，領護所攝，示總成規。
units.en: When the commander-in-chief set out and the guard of honor returned, they blocked the roads and cleared the way, moved like spirits at the reins, inspected all comings and goings, galloped about the carriage hub, drove and assigned sections, personally received the writing desk, led and protected what fell under their charge, and displayed the overall regulations.
units.literal: When the commander-in-chief set out his chariots and the guard of honor returned its banners, they blocked the roads and cleared the way, moved like spirits holding the reins, inspected comings and goings, galloped about the carriage hub, drove and assigned sections, personally received the writing desk, led and protected what was under their charge, and displayed the overall regulations.

units.zh: 若徵兵動衆，大興民役，行留之儀，請託在手，斷割牢稟，賣弄文符，捕叛追亡，長戍遠謪，軍有千齡之壽，室無百年之鬼，害政傷民，於此爲蠹。
units.en: When troops were levied and hosts mobilized, when corvée was raised on a great scale, the rites of going and staying lay in their hands through entreaty. They cut off prison rations, trafficked in written warrants, captured rebels and pursued fugitives, imposed long garrison service and distant exile. Armies seemed to live a thousand years while households had no ghost of a century — harming government and injuring the people, in this they were vermin.
units.literal: If troops were levied and hosts mobilized, if corvée was raised on a great scale, the rites of going and staying lay in their hands through entreaty; they cut off prison rations, trafficked in written warrants, captured rebels and pursued fugitives, imposed long garrison and distant exile; armies had the lifespan of a thousand years while households had no ghost of a hundred years — harming government and injuring the people, in this they were vermin.

units.zh: 況乎主幼時昏，其爲讒慝，亦何可勝紀也！
units.en: How much more when the ruler was young and the times benighted — their acts of slander and wickedness defy full reckoning!
units.literal: How much more when the ruler was young and the times benighted — their acts of slander and wickedness, how could they all be recorded!

units.zh: 贊曰：恩澤而侯，親倖爲舊。
units.en: The encomium says: Favored with grace and enfeoffed as lords — intimate trust was their ancient way.
units.literal: The encomium says: Favored with grace and enfeoffed as lords, intimate trust was their ancient way.

units.zh: 便煩左右，旣貴且富。
units.en: Useful at the ruler's side, they grew exalted and rich.
units.literal: Convenient at the ruler's side, they became both exalted and rich.
